extracted.intended_audience: writers seeking literary representation (adult/YA fiction, narrative nonfiction, memoir)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and wishlist from literary agent Hillary Jacobson (ICM Partners) about the types of manuscripts she is seeking and how to submit; aimed at authors preparing queries and sample pages. Includes genre preferences, tonal/structural desiderata, and submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General emotional and intellectual impact
rubrics_metrics.description: I read widely and am on the hunt for any and all writing that provokes a strong emotional reaction, adds an important perspective to the cultural conversation or forces the reader to challenge what they think. (Or ideally all of the above!)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a primary evaluative criterion: projects should move readers emotionally, contribute meaningfully to cultural discussion, or cause readers to rethink assumptions. No specific anti-patterns given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upmarket, literary, and commercial fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively building a list consisting of upmarket, literary, and commercial fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of favored contemporary titles: THE NEW ME, FRIENDS & STRANGERS, NORMAL PEOPLE, THE MOTHERS, GOODBYE VITAMIN, WHAT WE LOSE, HISTORY OF WOLVES, MARLENA. Read widely; be aware she represents both literary and commercial crossover work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction engaging contemporary social issues & modern female experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction that engages with contemporary social issues and the modern female experience, especially female coming of age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that examine topical social dynamics and female perspectives are prioritized. Examples provided in the list above illustrate tone and scope; she gravitates to stories that foreground female experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative nonfiction in the vein of high-profile essay/feature writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonfiction along the lines of TRICK MIRROR, THREE WOMEN, UNCANNY VALLEY or WITHOUT YOU, THERE IS NO US.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for narrative nonfiction that reads sharply and contributes to cultural conversation; examples indicate personal-essay driven or reportage-driven narrative nonfiction with strong voice and insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sweeping family saga with a compelling hook
rubrics_metrics.description: A sweeping family saga with a compelling hook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of favored books: ASK AGAIN YES, THE LAST ROMANTICS, PACHINKO, SAINTS FOR ALL OCCASIONS. The manuscript should offer scope, multiple relationships across time/generations, and a clear, marketable narrative hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculative fiction with a grounded twist
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculative fiction that features a world like ours with a twist or just a touch of the unreal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: THE IMMORTALISTS, STATION ELEVEN, SEVERANCE, THE AGE OF MIRACLES, NEVER LET ME GO. Preference for work that is rooted in recognizable reality but introduces speculative elements to explore themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upmarket witty romantic comedy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ONE TO WATCH, RED, WHITE & ROYAL BLUE, EVVIE DRAKE STARTS OVER. She favors romantic comedies with strong voice and commercial appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoirs structured like tightly plotted suspenseful fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoirs that read like tightly plotted and suspenseful fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: BRAIN ON FIRE, HOUSE IN THE SKY, WILD GAME, THE FACT OF A BODY. Preference for memoirs with narrative drive, tension, and craft comparable to fiction plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoirs of female empowerment / untold experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoirs of female empowerment that shine a light on untold experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: LAB GIRL, MAID, EDUCATED. Seeks memoirs that reveal new perspectives, particularly relating to women's lives and empowerment.

rubrics_metrics.name: True crime with immersive, thriller-like suspense
rubrics_metrics.description: True crime that feels as immersive and suspenseful as the best thrillers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: SAY NOTHING, I’LL BE GONE IN THE DARK, RED NOTICE. Prefers true crime that reads with narrative momentum and careful reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspense / 'secrets & lies' novels (dark & disturbing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspense, or what I like to call 'secrets & lies' novels. I definitely gravitate towards the dark and disturbing, and I love feeling unsettled…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think THE PERFECT NANNY, LITTLE FIRES EVERYWHERE, TANGERINE, THE EXPATRIATES, WATCH ME DISAPPEAR. Prefers psychological tension, secrecy, and morally ambiguous characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary suspense (serious/topical or playful/satirical)
rubrics_metrics.description: I want literary suspense as serious and topical as LONG BRIGHT RIVER, or as playful and satirical as SOCIAL CREATURE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open to literary suspense across tones—either socially urgent and serious or satirical and playful—so long as it retains literary ambition and suspense elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and #ownvoices; stories not set in the US
rubrics_metrics.description: #ownvoices! I’m committed to promoting underrepresented voices. I'm also always eager to read stories not set in the US.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively welcomes submissions from underrepresented authors and stories set outside the U.S.; explicitly values diverse perspectives and authentic representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-mindedness to unexpected submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: But sometimes I surprise myself with what I fall in love with, so please do query me even if your manuscript falls outside these guidelines!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages queries outside stated wishlist—she's open to being surprised. This reduces strict exclusionary interpretation of the listed preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: YA-specific preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: For YA: I am a sucker for anything that can be (accurately) pitched as GOSSIP GIRL meets X, like ANNA K or THE THOUSANDTH FLOOR... High-concept contemporary with a killer voice; Contemporary fantasy/speculative; Historical from unique perspectives and/or with a magical twist. Always a plus if you can subvert the tropes of the genre!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YA submissions should have a strong, pitchable hook ('Gossip Girl meets X'), distinctive voice, and may include contemporary high-concept premises, speculative elements, or inventive historical takes. Subverting genre tropes is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission protocol (format & contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Query Hillary at: hjacobson@icmpartners.com. Paste the first ten pages of your manuscript into the body of your email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: She states: 'I respond to every query, and my average response time is about a month.' Follow the specified submission format (first ten pages in email body) to comply with her process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association with film/TV and foreign rights (agent/agency capability)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICM Partners' New York literary agents work closely with ICM agents in Los Angeles to seek out opportunities for film and television adaptations. For foreign rights, ICM works in partnership with Curtis Brown in London...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not a manuscript-level criterion, this indicates the agency seeks projects with cross-media/translation potential; authors should be aware the agent actively pursues adaptation and foreign-rights opportunities.
